prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1388; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact at an intersection. The claimant reports a wrist fracture and is handling the claim without a lawyer. Assigned for initial review.

Entry 2: Confirmed the claimant is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the loss. No issues with coverage start have come up.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the collision the same way as in the first notice. The account has stayed consistent across every conversation so far.

Entry 4: Police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. The other driver's statement matches the claimant's description of how the crash happened.

Entry 5: Scene photographs were reviewed. The damage pattern is largely consistent with the side impact described and with the speeds involved.

Entry 6: No prior damage to the vehicle appears in our records or in the photos taken at inspection. Repair estimate requested from the shop.

Entry 7: The reported wrist fracture fits the kind of force expected from a side impact of this type. Medical records were requested from the treating provider.

Entry 8: Medical records show no earlier injury to the wrist or nearby body areas. Prior claims search returned nothing relevant.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Requested an updated treatment plan and a note from the treating physician explaining the timeline.

Entry 10: Physician's update received and reviewed. The timeline is within a reasonable range given the fracture type. Claim remains open pending final repair estimate and the physician's full report.
